findings.text: the base-arm row states the scratch tree is a scratch copy with the fixture at HEAD while the fixture in /tmp/reflex-base-arm.YBjbhm is byte-identical to bd231eff's (sha256 6bca468ea87254767da862ce820a38dfde142893c32a5b71bee5020d545c5d2e, 14802 bytes) and not to 45c9e428's: gate-arms.sh ran git show HEAD:tests/test_review_reflex_sweep.py at 12:28 while the worktree's HEAD was still bd231eff (the commit is 12:38:01), so it restored the base fixture, and under the row's stated configuration the arm would have been green because reckon/crew/recovery.py is identical at both revisions - the record's own configuration claim contradicts the 2 failed / 7 passed it reports.

the tests line repeats the misdescription above (fixture restored from HEAD) and adds that both failures IndexError at tests/test_review_reflex_sweep.py:331, where the baseline_suite.log the same sentence cites shows one IndexError at :331 and one AssertionError assert 2 == 1 at :276 (base-red.log shows the same two modes), so the sentence appears carried from the dispatch prompt rather than read from the log it names - and a promotion reads this line as the receipt for the suite delta.

the negative-control row names /tmp/reflex-negative-control.PmKkcL while the negative-control-red.log cited beside it as the receipt ran in /tmp/reflex-negative-control.997B9b, and the PmKkcL copy's test file differs from the reviewed head (its module docstring still carries the pre-final wording), so a reader who opens the tree the record names checks a fixture that is not the one reviewed.

the continuation this case proves depends on the refusal landing on the run list_live returns first, and the case pins no ordering: reversing runs.py:496's newest run id last would leave the case green (r-two dispatched, r-one refused) while the declared mutation stopped reddening it, so a production reordering silently downgrades the case from continuation to recording.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit - 45c9e428 is a single commit; the fixture gains the _live_claimant helper and both cases are rewritten to refuse through a scope claim, with two assertions strengthened rather than merely preserved (the refused run's identity, and that the refusal reason names the claiming run); reckon/crew/recovery.py carries no hunk because the accumulator already stored the report itself at recovery.py:1389.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when's five clauses are each in place - the module reports 9 passed exit 0, the log header names revision, tree and command, the declared mutation reddens the wave case, and both suite fields are log paths; I reproduced the head arm independently (9 passed) and applied the declared mutation myself to a fresh scratch copy of the head, where the wave case fails on assert 0 == 1 dispatched at tests/test_review_reflex_sweep.py:313 while the other eight pass (gates/rev-negative-control-own.log), and the added-failure derivation through the production read path measures 0 added ids over 2 base ids (gates/rev-added-failure-derivation.log).
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to make the sweep fixture's per-run review refusal reachable again through a path that still refuses; tests/test_review_reflex_sweep.py:182 writes a third live pointer holding a scope claim on the refused run's own review-record path, composed through recovery._review_dispatch_fields at reckon/crew/recovery.py:394, the refusal lands on the run the sweep enumerates first, and both named cases are green at head (9 passed, exit 0, gates/rev-head-module.log) and red at base (2 failed, 7 passed).
item_verdicts.manifest: well formed and complete, with resolvable suite logs and correct failure ids, and a negative_control_log that is a bare path whose first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim and whose mutation I verified exists byte-for-byte (head recovery.py plus one appended break line, 279596 against 279578 bytes); two of its prose claims about the base arm do not survive reading the log it cites, named in the findings below.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the five declared paths and the five paths in the diff coincide - recovery.py is declared and untouched; the two HTML docs are additive-only (55/0 and 42/0 lines); the figure directory contributes one renderer and one PNG; the 13 deleted lines in the range are all replaced lines in the test file.

justifications.durability: the wave case reddens under the declared mutation, reproduced in my own scratch tree, and the claimant-name assertion fails on any other refusal text; what is thinner is that the continuation it proves rests on list_live returning r-one first (runs.py:496), an ordering the case does not pin.
justifications.evidence: both arms and the declared mutation are recorded in logs whose headers name the revision, tree, command, module.__file__ and cwd, and I reproduced the head arm and the mutation arm myself; the deduction is for the manifest's and the landed record's description of the base arm, which the log it cites does not support.
justifications.fit: the helper follows the file's own fixture idiom (crew._write_json and crew.pointer_path, the _completed_pointer record shape), is named for the mechanism, carries no plan or ticket identifier in symbols or comments, and ruff check and ruff format --check are clean at base and head measured in place (gates/rev-lint-delta.log).
justifications.goal_fidelity: the refusal the fixture now produces is the production one (a live claim judged by reckon/crew/node.py:1338 and matched against the composed write path at recovery.py:394), both named cases are red at bd231eff and green at 45c9e428, and recovery.py needed no change because dispatch_awaiting_reviews already appended the report itself.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff is inside the declared fence, both HTML documents are additive-only with zero deletions, and no plan-version or plan-modified meta line is touched.
